Specifically, the compound is linked to Serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit beta isoform, which in turn is a target of N-[(3-hydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl)methyl]-7-methyloctanamide and Quinaldic Acid. These compounds are known to modulate ATP synthase activity, suggesting a possible mechanism by which the compound may influence the function of ATP synthase subunit a. The evidence is supported by multiple pathways, indicating a potential role in regulating ATP synthesis through interactions with this subunit. The strength of the evidence is moderate, with varying scores across the paths, but the consistent presence of multiple targets pointing to ATP synthase subunit a suggests a plausible biological relationship.
